\section{Overview}

\section{Declarations}

\begin{theorem}[Complement of PATH Lies in NL]
\lean{Complexity.compl_PATH_mem_NL}
\label{Complexity.compl_PATH_mem_NL}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.NL, Complexity.PATH, Complexity.PATH_mem_NL, Complexity.compl_mem_NL}
\difficulty{1}
The complement of the language $\mathrm{PATH}$ belongs to $\mathrm{NL}$, the class of
languages decidable by a nondeterministic Turing machine using logarithmic space.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Nondeterministic log space and its complement]
\lean{Complexity.NL_eq_coNL}
\label{Complexity.NL_eq_coNL}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.NL, Complexity.coNL, Complexity.compl_mem_NL}
\difficulty{3}
Let $\mathrm{NL}$ be the class of languages decidable by a finite nondeterministic
Turing machine using at most a constant multiple of $\lfloor\log_2 n\rfloor+1$ work-tape
cells on inputs of length $n$. Let $\mathrm{coNL}$ be the class of languages whose
complements belong to $\mathrm{NL}$. Then $\mathrm{NL}=\mathrm{coNL}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Closure of NSPACE under complement]
\lean{Complexity.NSPACE_compl_eq}
\label{Complexity.NSPACE_compl_eq}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.NSPACE, Complexity.SpaceConstructible, Complexity.compl_mem_NSPACE}
\difficulty{3}
For every space-constructible function $S:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$, the class of binary
languages whose complements belong to $\mathrm{NSPACE}(S)$ is exactly
$\mathrm{NSPACE}(S)$.
\end{theorem}
